title: [IELTS INSIGHTS JAN 26] - Postgraduate course fees in three countries: 2007
prompt: The table below shows the postgraduate course fees in US Dollars that international students paid in three countries in 2007. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table gives information about living costs and fees for four courses in three countries, A, B, and C.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, courses in countries B and C charged substantially higher fees than those in country A. Additionally, computing and science were the most expensive courses in all three countries, with country B charging the highest fees for these two subjects.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding countries B and C, students in country B paid the highest fees, with being charged 29,000 USD for science and 27,000 USD for computing, while the figures for country B were 25,000 USD and 24,000 USD, respectively. As for arts and commerce, students in countries B and C were charged 18,000 USD and 19,000 USD respectively for both courses, while meals & accommodation were far cheaper in B than C, at 17,000 USD and 11,000 USD, respectively.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Turning to country A, it offered the most affordable fees across all subjects and services. Science and computing, despite being the most expensive subjects in country A, cost students 11,000 USD each to enroll, less than half the corresponding fees in countries B and C. The lowest fees were charged for the remaining courses, arts and commerce, as well as meals and accommodation, all costing 8,000 USD each.
